defect.title: Overwrite's new `TType extends object` gate takes both branches when the base context is `any`, so a middleware that extends ctx turns an `any` context into a union that rejects access to any property the middleware didn't add
defect.trigger: Declare the root context as `any`, either with `initTRPC.context<any>()` or with a createContext typed `() => Promise<any>` passed as `initTRPC.context<typeof createContext>()`. Then add a middleware that extends ctx (`next({ ctx: { user } })`) and read any property on ctx in a later resolver that the middleware did not add (e.g. `ctx.req`, `ctx.foo`).
defect.consequence: tsc fails with TS2339 "Property 'foo' does not exist on type '{ user: number; } | { [x: string]: any; [x: number]: any; [x: symbol]: any; } | ...'". The same code compiles cleanly at the merge-base (10.43.2 semantics), so this is a type-level compatibility break shipped in the 10.43.3 patch release. A procedure without a middleware, or a middleware that doesn't extend ctx, is unaffected.
defect.evidence: Standalone tsc 5.1.3 harness (clone's own binary) over copies of packages/server/src at the merge-base, at the head, and at the head with #5039's utils.ts/types.ts (de858987) swapped in. probe.ts case A `initTRPC.context<any>().create().procedure.use(({next}) => next({ctx:{user:1}})).query(({ctx}) => ctx.foo)`: merge-base has no probe errors; head gives TS2339 on '{ user: number; } | { [x: string]: any; ... }'; the #5039 fix gives TS2339 on '{ user: number; } | { user: number; } | { user: number; }'. probe2.ts case G (createContext returns Promise<any>, isAuthed adds user, resolver reads ctx.req.headers) gives the same pattern. The controls (context<any> without a middleware, an object context with a middleware, next() without a ctx override, reading the added key) compile at all three. #5039 and v10.45.2 and current main all keep a `TType extends object` gate, so the behaviour was never fixed upstream. No downstream issue report was found (GitHub search API).
defect.required_outcome: When the incoming context (TType) is `any`, overwriting it with a middleware's ctx extension must give a type that still allows access to arbitrary properties while typing the added keys, as the merge-base did (`{ [x: string]: any; user: number }`), not a union containing the bare extension. Code that compiled at 10.43.2 in this shape must compile again. This must hold together with GT-j1's required outcomes.
manifestations: TS2339 on reading a non-extended ctx property after a ctx-extending middleware when the root context is `any` (initTRPC.context<any>() or a createContext returning any)

rulings.reasoning: True at the head, clean at the merge-base: the head's `Overwrite<TType, TWith> = TType extends object ? (...) : (TType extends any ? (TWith extends any ? TWith : TType) : never)` resolves both arms when TType is `any` (a conditional whose check type is `any` gives the union of both arms), and one of those arms is the bare `TWith` = `{ user: number }`. The merge-base's single `TType extends any ? ...` gate only takes the true arm for `any`. Reproduced: head `probe.ts(7,27): error TS2339: Property 'foo' does not exist on type '{ user: number; } | { [x: string]: any; [x: number]: any; [x: symbol]: any; } | { [x: string]: any; [x: number]: any; [x: symbol]: any; }'`; merge-base has no probe.ts errors. The PR introduced it, since the diff only changed the outer gate. Not a duplicate of GT-j1: GT-j1's trigger is an unconstrained generic type parameter flowing into ProcedureParams, and its required outcome is checked against issue-5037's test, which #5039 (de858987) satisfies. At de858987 this claim still fails: `probe.ts(7,27): error TS2339: Property 'foo' does not exist on type '{ user: number; } | { user: number; } | { user: number; }'`. So a fix sufficient for GT-j1 does not restore this outcome, and by the rubric that makes it a separate defect. It isn't covered by any non_defect either: the index-signature entry concerns the unchanged mapped-type body; this concerns the new gate. It is material because it is a reproduced compatibility break in a patch release on a public API shape (`context<any>` or an any-returning createContext plus an auth-style middleware), with a concrete compile failure. Counter-argument: `any` context is an opt-out escape hatch, no user reported this in the roughly three years since, and upstream's own fix and current main keep the same gate, which suggests low real-world impact or tacit acceptance. I accept that this lowers severity but not materiality. Code that compiled in 10.43.2 stops compiling in 10.43.3, the rubric accepts an adjudicator's own reproduction as demonstrated consequence, and nothing in the record shows the maintainers deliberately chose this behaviour. #5039's degenerate `{user}|{user}|{user}` result looks like an unnoticed artifact, not a design decision.
